items.title: It is time for psychology to consider disability as diversity
items.author: William B. Meese
items.content: Disabled people comprise the world’s largest minority group, but they remain marginalized within psychology. To address historical harms and improve psychological science, researchers must understand the social construction of disability, centre disability in research and prioritize representation across the field.

items.title: Rethinking handedness as a spectrum in clinical work and basic research
items.author: Marietta Papadatou-Pastou
items.content: People with mental health conditions frequently show handedness phenotypes that fall between traditional left- and right-handedness. In this Review, Papadatou-Pastou coins the term ‘flux-handedness’ to capture the complexity of handedness, including degree, direction and consistency, thereby enabling more precise research and clinical insights.
